Senses.Explanation: Literally, a cloth shirt from Qingzhou. In the Chan record it is Zhaozhou's stock answer to the question, "the ten thousand things return to one; where does the one return?": "I made a cloth shirt in Qingzhou; it weighs seven pounds." Later records call this the "Qingzhou cloth-shirt case" (青州布衫話), quote the seven-pound formula, ask whether the assembly has finished or taken off its Qingzhou shirt, and compare it with the patched robe actually worn by those present. The shirt is therefore not merely a place-name garment in this corpus: it is the named object and shorthand of Zhaozhou's recorded answer. The texts provide no additional gloss for the answer, and neither does this entry.
Senses.Note: 216 occurrences in 104 allowlisted texts. The full formula and its later deployments are one object, not separate interpretive senses.
